structure.summary: The text is a letter from Tata Consumer Products Limited dated May 22, 2025, addressed to National Stock Exchange, BSE, and Calcutta Stock Exchange, regarding the submission of the Integrated Annual Report for FY 2024-25 under SEBI Regulation 34(1). It references a prior letter about the 62nd AGM scheduled for June 18, 2025, via video conference. structure.title: Chairman’s message
structure.summary: This chairman's message addresses the evolving global economic landscape, including policy uncertainty, trade shifts, and India's resilient growth outlook. It highlights consumer trends like premiumisation, health & wellness, convenience, quick commerce, and the growing influence of Gen Z and Millennials. The message outlines Tata Consumer's ambition to become a full-fledged FMCG company, detailing its financial performance (16% revenue growth to ₹17,618 Crores, 8% EBITDA growth to ₹2,502 Crores, negative net working capital), portfolio transformation through acquisitions (Organic India, Capital Foods) and growth businesses (28% of India revenue), distribution expansion (4.4 million outlets), digital and AI integration, and international success (UK's #2 branded tea). It also covers sustainability commitments under 'Better Sourcing, Planet, Communities, Nutrition' aligned with Project Aalingana, and concludes with gratitude to stakeholders.

structure.title: Tata Consumer Products MD & CEO Message and Financial Performance
structure.summary: The page includes the MD & CEO's message, which discusses the company's five-year transformation into a multi-category FMCG company with a portfolio spanning tea, coffee, water, RTD, food staples, breakfast cereals, snacks, mini meals, cooking aids, condiments, and herbal supplements. It highlights the theme 'Growing Together. For Better,' the integration of Tata Chemicals' salt and foods business, and the development of capabilities in sales, distribution, innovation, digitalisation, and supply chain. The page also presents financial highlights under 'Consistent Performance with Steady Growth': a 14.2% EBITDA margin, revenue from operations of INR 17,618 Crores (up 16% from INR 15,206 Crores in FY24), 29% growth in India Foods, and 10% growth in India Beverages, with footnotes defining these segments.

structure.title: TRANSFORMING THE PORTFOLIO, EXPANDING THE ADDRESSABLE MARKET
structure.summary: The text outlines Tata Consumer Products' strategy, portfolio transformation, and distribution strength. It details evolution into a multi-category F&B company with core businesses (tea, coffee, salt) and growth vectors (Sampann, NourishCo, Soulfull, Capital Foods, Organic India) now 28% of India business. It addresses consumer trends—Health & Wellness, Convenience, Premiumisation—with new launches and acquisitions. International expansion includes premium Tetley and teapigs offerings and Organic India's global presence. Distribution covers 275 million households via 4.4 million outlets, with rural/urban network expansion, split routes, new channel incubation, omnichannel strategy, and a next-gen Go-to-Market platform for salesforce productivity.

structure.title: ACCELERATING INNOVATION
structure.summary: The text covers the MD & CEO's message on accelerating innovation with a higher innovation-to-sales ratio and a nutrition policy, unlocking value from recent acquisitions (Capital Foods and Organic India) through integration and synergy, strengthening international business with improved profitability and market positions, embedding sustainability via the 'For Better Living' strategy and ESG targets, nurturing talent through development and engagement, and creating enduring value, concluding with gratitude to stakeholders.

structure.title: Sustainability, Talent, and Enduring Value in Annual Report
structure.summary: This page from Tata Consumer Products' Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 includes a continuation of the MD & CEO's message, highlighting sustainability achievements such as inclusion in the S&P Global Sustainability Yearbook 2025, a 15% improvement in ESG risk rating, and recognition as 'Most Sustainable Consumer Goods Company (India)' and No.2 in Business World's IMSC rankings. It details the 'For Better Living' sustainability strategy with four pillars, ESG targets for 2026 and long-term ambitions for 2030/2040. The page also covers nurturing talent through career growth, leadership pipeline, and Growth Mindset Behaviours, and concludes with creating enduring value through Tata Group values, infrastructure, portfolio, brands, and innovation, ending with the MD & CEO's gratitude.

structure.title: Business Strategy, Supply Chain Resilience, and Sustainability Initiatives
key_items: SUPPLY CHAIN RESILIENCE; SUSTAINABILITY FOCUS AND CLIMATE ACTION
structure.summary: The page covers the business landscape and strategic agility to drive growth amid evolving consumer preferences, technology, regulations, and macroeconomic volatility. It addresses supply chain resilience, detailing approaches to mitigate geopolitical tensions, trade restrictions, commodity price volatility, inflation, and exchange rate fluctuations through supplier partnerships, diversified sourcing, inventory management, AI/ML forecasting, and digital solutions. It also covers sustainability focus and climate action, including embedding ESG principles, circular economy initiatives, carbon footprint reduction, renewable energy, and progress against FY 2026 targets. The page includes corporate portrait and business momentum sections.

structure.title: Strategic Priorities: Digital AI, Premiumisation, Health and Wellness
structure.summary: The page outlines three strategic focus areas for an FMCG company. First, digital and AI-led transformation is reshaping the industry through predictive analytics for demand forecasting, supply chain optimisation, and AI-powered personalisation for consumer engagement, illustrated by Tata Tea campaigns. Second, premiumisation and value-added offerings are driven by rising incomes and aspirational consumers, with approaches including expanding premium product portfolios, accelerating innovation, and targeted marketing. Third, health and wellness-led consumption reflects growing demand for natural, organic, and functional products, addressed by expanding the health and wellness portfolio, embedding nutrition in innovation, and acquiring brands like Organic India and Tata Soulfull. Each section includes a brief 'Our Approach' with specific initiatives and examples.

structure.title: Omnichannel, Demographics, and M&A Strategy
key_items: OMNICHANNEL GROWTH AND EVOLVING RETAIL LANDSCAPE
structure.summary: The page covers omnichannel growth and the evolving retail landscape, highlighting e-commerce, quick commerce, and D2C trends, with an approach of digital expansion and optimizing physical distribution. It addresses changing consumer demographics, focusing on Millennials and Gen Z preferences for authenticity, transparency, and sustainability, and the approach of portfolio expansion and digital marketing. Finally, it discusses M&A and strategic collaborations as growth drivers, including evaluating acquisitions, integrating Capital Foods and Organic India, and partnerships like Ching's Secret and Kurkure, while unlocking synergies in acquired businesses.

key_items: ACCELERATED GROWTH MOMENTUM IN TEA BUSINESS
CELEBRATING INDIA AND ITS DIVERSE CULTURE

It covers hyper-local marketing campaigns, cultural celebrations, festive packs, and community initiatives, including partnerships and donations. The document also mentions relaunches, new product launches, and regional campaigns, emphasizing market share growth, premiumisation, and digital presence.

structure.title: LEADING WITH AI
structure.summary: This text highlights AI-driven marketing campaigns by Tata Tea brands: Tata Tea Gold VitaCare's mirror insert and AI 'Face Test' for vitamin D awareness; Agni's AI rural campaign 'Mere Ghar Ki Agni' using WhatsApp video intelligence; Tata Tea Kanan Devan's AI expression matching at Thrissur Pooram; and Tata Tea Gold Care's personalized Mother's Day packs. It also covers Josh 2.0 by Tata Tea Agni leveraging YouTube to celebrate homemakers, and Tata Tea Gemini's education drive against adulterated loose tea. Additionally, it details Tata Coffee's expansion, crossing INR 100 Crores in gross revenue, diversifying with Tata Coffee Grand and premium Tata Coffee Gold (Hazelnut, Vanilla flavors), and launching Filter Coffee Decoction in three regional flavors.

structure.title: BREWING IT RIGHT
structure.summary: The text covers Tata Coffee Grand's International Coffee Day collaboration with Times of India to distribute aroma-infused newspapers, and the launch of a Tamil Nadu coffee anthem by Santhosh Narayanan. It then details Tata Salt's leadership expansion through rural footprint growth, premium portfolio innovation, and market development, including the Himalayan Rock Salt campaign. Key metrics include a 30bps salt market share increase, 8% salt revenue growth, and 15% five-year CAGR. Value-added salts are noted for growing salience in health-focused consumer choices, reinforcing Tata Salt's trusted position.

structure.title: STRENGTHENING BRAND EQUITY
structure.summary: The text covers Tata Consumer Products' brand equity strengthening for Tata Salt, highlighting record-high brand health indicators and a focused marketing approach. It details campaigns: Tamil Nadu's Tata Salt Crystal emphasizing quality, the Himalayan Rock Salt campaign with Kajol establishing 'Desh ka No.1 Rock Salt', and the IPL 2024 'Namak Ho Tata ka, Tata Namak' campaign with 11 films reviving the iconic jingle. It also covers expanding value-added offerings with 31% revenue growth in value-added salts and 57% volume growth in rock salt, plus the relaunch of Tata Salt Iron Health (double fortified with Iron and Iodine) at an accessible price and the reintroduction of Tata Salt Sendha+ in the mass-premium range.

structure.title: Tata Sampann: Elevating Everyday Nutrition and Building a Premium Brand
key_items: ELEVATING EVERYDAY NUTRITION WITH TATA SAMPANN
BUILDING TATA SAMPANN INTO A PREMIUM TRUSTED INDIAN FOOD BRAND
structure.summary: The page covers Tata Sampann's strategy to elevate everyday nutrition and build a premium trusted Indian food brand. It highlights the underpenetrated packaged foods market, Tata Sampann's focus on quality, authenticity, and convenience, strategic investments in product availability, category expansion, and consumer engagement. It details the brand's expansion into dry fruits, nuts, and cold-pressed oils, and presents revenue growth figures showing 29% growth and a five-year CAGR of 31%. The page also discusses e-commerce leadership and the 'Pyaar Bhara' masterbrand campaign featuring chefs Sanjeev Kapoor and Ranveer Brar, which aims to strengthen brand recall, build trust, and showcase diverse offerings like unpolished dal, Sunehri Peeli Haldi, Khushbhudaar Hing, and High-Fibre Gurjari Poha across multiple touchpoints.

structure.title: Tata Sampann and Tata Soulfull Innovation, Millets and Category Expansion
key_items: INTRODUCING NEW FORMATS FOR CONVENIENCE AND NUTRITION
STRENGTHENING PRESENCE IN EIGHT CATEGORIES, AFTER ENTERING THREE NEW CATEGORIES IN FY25
structure.summary: The page highlights Tata Consumer Products' innovation-led strategy for Tata Sampann and Tata Soulfull. Tata Sampann's new convenience and nutrition formats include premium dry fruits, Easy Cook Ragi Atta (100% ragi, no maida, rich in fibre, calcium, iron), Easy Cook Kabuli Channa (no overnight soaking), expanded cold-pressed oils, and whole spices. Innovation-to-sales ratio figures across FY23-FY25 are shown. Tata Soulfull democratises millets under its 'Desh Ke Millets' vision, achieving 5X revenue growth since its 2021 acquisition and reach of 600k outlets, with breakfast and snacking portfolios for kids and adults. It strengthened presence in eight categories after entering three new ones in FY25, listing core portfolio and new millet-based launches.

structure.title: Tata Soulfull's Innovation, Millet Expansion, and Growth Strategy
key_items: EXPANDING BEYOND THE BREAKFAST PORTFOLIO- MILLET-BASED SNACKING
ACHIEVING CONSISTENT GROWTH ACROSS KEY CATEGORIES
structure.summary: The page highlights Tata Consumer Products' strategy to strengthen core and accelerate growth businesses. It details consumer innovations like Masala Muesli, Corn Flakes+, and Masala Oats+ Dal Shakti, and expansion into millet-based snacking with No Maida Rusk and Ragi Bites Wafers. It discusses making millets mainstream through Tata Soulfull leveraging distribution, retail partnerships (e.g., Reliance Retail), and consumer engagement, achieving 1.5X market share in modern trade over two years. It also notes consistent growth: 1.5X urban market share in two years, 2X general trade market share since launch, and No. 2 position in flavoured oats within a year.

structure.title: BUILDING A RESILIENT AND SCALABLE READY-TO-DRINK BUSINESS
structure.summary: The text outlines the strategy and growth of Tata Consumer Products' Ready-To-Drink (RTD) business, focusing on strengthening core and growth areas. It highlights the resilient and scalable RTD business model, innovation pipeline, and hydration play. Tata Copper+ grew 18% and became Air India's hydration partner. The premium portfolio led by Himalayan contributes 11% to RTD. Innovations include Tetley Kombucha, Alkaline Water, Tata Gluco+ Sports Drink relaunch, Tata Gluco+ Jelly Drink, and Tata Coffee Grand Cold Coffee. Consumer connect efforts include pan-India presence for Tata Gluco+ Cup, hyper-local marketing, and digital engagement. Distribution strategies involve increasing numeric distribution, implementing a Distributor Management System, expanding in quick commerce, e-commerce, modern trade, and pharmacy outlets, and structured programs in HoReCa and small-format modern trade.

structure.title: DRIVING PROFITABLE GROWTH IN INTERNATIONAL MARKETS
key_items: STRENGTHENING MARKET LEADERSHIP IN THE UK
structure.summary: The text covers International business growth in South Africa and the Middle East, driven by mass sampling, premiumisation, innovation, and execution. It reports a 16.5% FY 2025 EBITDA margin. It highlights Tata Consumer Products becoming the #2 branded tea player in the UK, with growth across Tetley, teapigs, and Good Earth, supported by shopper engagement, sampling, and coupon campaigns. In the USA, Eight O’Clock coffee maintained stable market share. The document also references delivering on strategy, corporate portrait, business momentum, and strengthening core and accelerating growth businesses.

structure.title: DRIVING GROWTH IN THE USA
structure.summary: Eight O'Clock Coffee's humorous 'Have it Black' campaign promoted drinking coffee black. teapigs saw exceptional US growth, with 38.5% sales increase at Whole Foods and Cold Brew Peach & Mango as a 2025 trend. In Canada, Tetley transitioned to sustainable packaging, was voted most trusted tea brand for the fifth year, and retained market leadership. The 'Taste of Home' campaign raised awareness of Tata products in Canada, using videos, influencers, and promotions to achieve nearly 14.5 million impressions, with Tata Tea the fastest-growing tea brand in the ethnic channel.

structure.title: DRIVING MOMENTUM ACROSS OTHER INTERNATIONAL MARKETS
structure.summary: The text covers international market momentum: South Africa's strong performance via distribution gains, product innovation (Laager Plus CBD, Tetley Chai Latte), and retail partnerships; the Middle East's third consecutive year of growth through Saudi expansion, strategic activations, and new products (Tata Soulfull, Tata Tea Kanan Devan). It details premium and wellness offerings: teapigs All Day Brew, Tetley Chai Latte, and UK black teas inspired by British bakes (Mint & Chocolate, Lemon Drizzle, Digestive biscuit). It outlines strategy to unlock Capital Foods and Organic India potential, build Food Services and Pharma channels, and expand into adjacencies and whitespaces. Capital Foods initiatives include white space expansion, training 200+ distributor reps, Food Services channel development, and INR 799 Crores revenue. New products: Hakka Noodles with Masala Sachet, Sriracha sauces, Schezwan Ketchup, Momo Chutney, Fried Rice Masala, and consideration of value-accretive inorganic opportunities.

structure.title: Capital Foods Growth Initiatives and White Space Expansion
structure.summary: The page highlights Capital Foods' growth momentum through targeted innovation, market expansion, and strategic brand collaborations. Key initiatives include expanding into white spaces to grow the addressable market, training over 200 Distributor Sales Representatives to improve retail execution, and developing the Food Services channel for deeper engagement with commercial kitchens. Capital Foods revenue stands at INR 799 Crores. New product launches in white spaces include Hakka Noodles with Masala Sachet, Sriracha Hot and Green Chilli Sauces, Schezwan Ketchup, Momo Chutney, and Fried Rice Masala. The page also mentions building on new opportunities, unlocking potential of Capital Foods and Organic India, building Food Services and Pharma channels, expanding into portfolio adjacencies, and considering value-accretive inorganic opportunities.

key_items: STRENGTHENING BRAND EQUITY THROUGH A MULTI-CHANNEL APPROACH
KURKURE X CHING’S SECRET – A POWER PACKED BRAND COLLABORATION

It covers the Kurkure x Ching's Secret limited-edition Schezwan Chutney launch backed by a nationwide TV, digital, and print campaign featuring Ranveer Singh and Sara Ali Khan. It also details Smith & Jones' expansion bringing international flavors in convenient formats, including new Pizza and Pasta sauce, plus report sections like Corporate Portrait, Business Momentum, and statutory and sustainability reporting.

structure.title: ORGANIC INDIA – STRENGTHENING AND SCALING THE BRAND
key_items: GROWING THE PHARMA CHANNEL; UNLOCKING POTENTIAL IN ORGANIC FOODS; RESEARCH-DRIVEN WELLNESS PORTFOLIO EXPANSION
structure.summary: The text details Organic India's strategy to scale the brand, leveraging Tata Consumer Products' distribution and new channels like pharmacy, building a global organic brand, and future-proofing through innovation. It highlights revenue of INR 374 crores, a refreshed global brand architecture with unified visual identity and Tata masterbrand endorsement, and expansion in the pharmacy channel via expert content and in-store investments. It covers unlocking potential in organic foods, research-driven wellness portfolio expansion with new launches (Khandsari Sugar, Gokshura, gummies, lattes) and R&D partnerships, strengthening brand equity through campaigns and influencer collaborations, and international expansion with e-commerce, D2C, and new products like Ashwagandha Gummies and Fair Trade supplements.

structure.title: INCUBATING CHANNELS OF THE FUTURE
structure.summary: The text outlines Tata Consumer Products' incubation of two future-ready channels: Pharma and Food Service, to drive long-term growth. The Pharma channel focuses on Organic India's expansion into pharmacies with nutraceuticals and herbal infusions, following a successful pilot in ten cities, now rolling out across 40 markets with presence in key chains like Medplus, Wellness Forever, and Noble Plus. The Food Service channel targets HoReCa, corporate canteens, and B2B partners to expand the Capital Foods portfolio, with a successful pilot in Mumbai and Ahmedabad leading to phased expansion across 16 cities, developing customized bulk product formats and engaging institutional buyers for sustained growth.

structure.summary: The page covers the Coffee and Tea Vending business, incubated in 2024, which offers premium beverages via bean-to-cup and filter machines, leveraging coffee sourcing expertise, state-of-the-art machines, and a wide branded tea portfolio for a one-stop solution. It highlights consumer-first innovations like filter/chai machines, achieving 7x YoY growth and 5%+ market share in bean-to-cup. The Solubles B2B business, integrated with Tata Consumer Products, delivers instant coffee and tea, demonstrating resilience amid commodity price rises, leveraging consumption trends in health/wellness and value blends, and expanding in Africa and the Middle East. Synergies from integration include robust sales and cross-selling. Sustainability efforts include renewable energy (solar at Toopran, wind/solar at Theni), biomass boilers for circularity at Munnar and Vietnam, and water reduction at Vietnam.

structure.title: EXPANDING THE ‘THIRD PLACE’ EXPERIENCE WITH STARBUCKS
structure.summary: Tata Starbucks, India's largest café operator, is expanding its 'Third Place' experience through diverse store formats, innovative offerings, and immersive customer experiences, aiming for 1,000 stores with a focus on Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. It has grown to over 479 stores across 80 cities, deepening penetration in these tiers. Innovative formats include a Metro Station Store in Mumbai, Coffee Experiential Stores in New Delhi and Mumbai, a Pet-Friendly Store in Jaipur, and a Greener Store in Ludhiana with sustainable elements. The text also notes store count growth from 185 in FY20 to 479 in FY25, and city footprint expansion from 11 to 80 cities over the same period.

structure.title: Starbucks India Product Innovations and Cultural Campaigns
key_items: ENERGISING INDIA WITH COFFEE FLAVOURS CURATED WITH CARE
structure.summary: The page outlines Starbucks India's strategy, corporate portrait, business momentum, and new opportunities, followed by two main sections. First, it details product innovations: Monsooned Malabar reserve coffee, summer Cold Brew and Refreshers (Kiwi Calamansi, Lychee Raspberry), Diwali festive treats with Bombay Sweet Shop, and a Classics Menu for the 12-year milestone featuring regional coffee and Indian-flavored food. Second, it covers hyperlocal campaigns: 'Brewed to a 100' celebrating the 100th Mumbai store with Imagine Foods and Anamika Khanna, the Diwali 360 '#MeriSpecialJagah' initiative with gift hampers and festive beverages, and the Classics Menu campaign with the tagline 'Classic Fix for Your Pakao Situation'. Financial statements and reports are also referenced.

structure.title: MAKING WOMEN FEEL HAPPIER, SAFER
structure.summary: Starbucks advances gender inclusivity with women-focused stores prioritizing safety, mentorship, and professional development, earning Tata Starbucks recognition as a best workplace for women in India. Tata Consumer Products strengthens distributor management with the MAVIC Go-To-Market platform, reducing onboarding time and improving efficiency. The company expands sales infrastructure with over 1,200 new hires, 100 additional super-stockists, and direct reach growing to 2.0 million, while completing MAVIC rollout across thousands of distributors. Rural network expansion includes augmenting the rural sales organization and reorganizing the wholesale channel to maintain product availability and drive volume.

structure.title: SHARPER URBAN FOCUS
key_items: Split Routes Driving Focus; Tech-enabled superior execution
structure.summary: The text outlines a sharper urban focus strategy for large cities, detailing split routes across metros and towns over 500,000 population to enhance sales coverage, with dedicated salesforces for beverages, packaged foods, and new-age brands. It covers tech-enabled execution, driving assortment, per dealer offtake (PDO), and DSR productivity, including a timeline from 2022 to 2024: splitting DSR routes across beverages and foods, then three ways post-acquisition of Capital Foods and Organic India, achieving 100% split routes in large towns. It also lists expanding direct coverage, driving more lines and NPDs, higher per dealer offtake, relevant promos, real-time incentive tracking, and 100% deployment of MAVIC distributor management system.

structure.title: Strategic Channels, Modern Trade, ARS, and Process Efficiency
key_items: ENHANCED EMPHASIS ON CHANNELS OF THE FUTURE
structure.summary: The page covers the company's strategic initiatives: enhancing channels of the future by expanding in modern trade, e-commerce, and quick commerce to reach diverse consumers. Modern trade efforts include alliances with regional chains like Vijeta, Ratnadeep, and Vishal Megamart, achieving 18% growth. E-commerce and quick commerce have grown 57%, maintaining leadership in tea and premium green tea/herbal segments, and driving premiumization with growth in rock salt, freeze-dried coffee, and care variants. It also details implementing an Automatic Replenishment System (ARS) across rural and urban areas to improve SKU availability and reduce stockouts, and highlights improved process efficiency through ARS, which reduces manual workload, aligns demand with replenishment, improves service metrics, and optimizes distributor ROI.

structure.title: Tata Consumer Products Vision, Mission, Values and Strategy
key_items: THE TATA CONSUMER PRODUCTS’ NORTH STAR
structure.summary: The page presents Tata Consumer Products' North Star, which aligns employees around six Strategic Pillars, ambition to be the premier global FMCG company and No. 1 F&B player, vision of building better lives and thriving communities, mission of passionately growing and transforming everyday, and core values of empathy, integrity, agility, excellence, and ownership. It outlines the strategy to action through six pillars: strengthening core and accelerating growth businesses, driving execution excellence, building new opportunities, creating a future-ready organization, driving digital and innovation, and embedding sustainability. It also details Growth Mindset Behaviours, including consumer-centricity, trailblazing execution, ownership, continuous improvement, and living the Tata Code of Conduct.

structure.title: Tata Consumer Products: Leadership, Adaptive Organisation, and Future-Ready Capability
key_items: CHARTING A PATHWAY FROM ‘GOOD TO GREAT’
DEVELOPING CAPACITY AND CAPABILITY FOR A FUTURE-READY BUSINESS
structure.summary: The page covers Tata Consumer Products' strategy delivery through three sections. 'Charting a Pathway from Good to Great' details the Senior Leadership Forum (launched May 2024, second edition January 2025, plus a virtual edition) uniting 150+ leaders to shape future direction, assess outcomes, refine ways of working, strengthen strategic alignment, encourage cross-functional collaboration, and reinforce commitment to the TCP North Star. 'Building an Adaptive Organisation' addresses regular organisational reviews aligned to strategic pillars, integrating acquired businesses (Capital Foods, Organic India, Tata Coffee, Tata Soulfull, NourishCo, Tata SmartFoodz), and blending multi-legacy, multi-generational organisations into a cohesive, inclusive, future-ready culture. 'Developing Capacity and Capability for a Future-Ready Business' covers investing in capacity and capabilities, streamlining processes, upskilling talent, and implementing new operating models including the 6-cluster India Sales structure, USA Direct Sales model, and category-based QARA organisation in India.

structure.title: Building a Future-Ready Organisation Through Culture, Talent, and Leadership
structure.summary: The page outlines Tata Consumer Products' approach to becoming future-ready through three sections. Cultural Convergence describes weaving a strong cultural fabric that celebrates diversity and shared values without imposing uniformity. Becoming an Employer of Choice emphasizes attracting, developing, and retaining diverse talent as a key differentiator. Emerging Leaders Plus details a 12-month management trainee programme in India that hires merit-based candidates, provides cross-functional exposure and Executive Committee interaction, and reached over 3,200 students across 100+ campuses within 48 hours on LinkedIn.

structure.title: Talent Development, Internal Mobility, and Leadership Growth Initiatives
structure.summary: The page covers Tata Consumer's talent development and leadership growth initiatives. It highlights the 'Growing Beyond Better' Business Challenge Competition, which attracted 13,400 registrations from 472 B-School campuses, connecting with bright minds. It also details Tata Global Internships in international markets like the US and UK. Internal mobility is emphasized through structured assessments and pathways for horizontal and vertical career progression, with 36% of leadership pipeline employees taking on new roles in the past year. Finally, 'Trailblazers' Tracks' showcases leadership pipeline candidates' journeys, reflecting focus on internal talent development, career mobility, and continuous learning.

structure.title: Future-Ready Organisation: Skills, Leadership, and Frontline Development
structure.summary: The page outlines strategies to build a future-ready organisation. It emphasises skill enhancement for competitive advantage, with a focus on digital and functional expertise. Leadership development is prioritised through in-house programmes with TMTC and global institutions, with over 40% of the leadership pipeline participating. Aarohan strengthens frontline managerial capabilities via three pillars: Leading Self, Leading Teams, and Driving Change & Results. Self-awareness is fostered using SHL's 360° Feedback Survey and OPQ for senior leaders. Skill Up! builds functional expertise across Sales, Operations, Finance, Marketing, and Digital, driving a future-focused learning agenda. The page also includes report navigation links and performance highlights.

structure.title: EMBEDDING GROWTH MINDSET BEHAVIOURS
structure.summary: The text discusses embedding Growth Mindset Behaviours (GMB) at Tata Consumer Products to support its goal of becoming a premier global FMCG company. It explains that GMBs are aligned with the company's five values and are intended to differentiate the organization and shape stakeholder experiences. The efforts aim to embed these behaviours organization-wide for unified action, foster an enabling, collaborative, and winning culture for long-term value creation, and engage colleagues through culture books, videos, leadership conversations, and special sessions. Additional sections cover delivering on strategy, corporate portrait, business momentum, digital innovation, and strategic differentiators, including being the leading innovation-driven FMCG player in India.

Key metrics include a 5.2% innovation-to-sales ratio, 15% disruptive innovation, 5X innovation revenue versus FY21, and 150 launches in four years with 3-4 new launches per month in FY25. The nutrition policy is built on three pillars—Superior Experiences, Nutritionally Enhanced Offerings, and Sustenance—creating a portfolio catering to indulgence and functional benefits. It also details leveraging consumer trends: 12 health and wellness launches, 14 premiumisation launches, and 15 convenience launches.

structure.title: Innovation, Science-Backed Products, and Sustainable Packaging Initiatives
structure.summary: The page covers embedding disruptive innovation through reimagined everyday products with improved nutrition, convenience, and ingredient-led innovation, including nutritious millet flour for easy rotis, no-soak faster-cooking legumes, jowar-infused healthier snacking, and brew-free low-unit-pack options. It highlights science-backed innovation for differentiated products using consumer insights, sensory evaluations, and analytical science for superior nutrition and credible claims, exemplified by Tata Sampann Unpolished Toor Dal retaining micronutrients. It also details Tata LYFE+ Alkaline water's distinctive packaging developed with Tata Elxsi for a premium aesthetic, and Tata Copper+ value engineering with a redesigned neck and cap reducing PET usage by about 30%, eliminating 1,200 metric tons annually, reinforcing sustainability.

structure.title: STRENGTHENING ACADEMIA COLLABORATIONS
structure.summary: The text covers Tata Consumer Products' strategic academic partnerships through MoUs with NIFTEM for food processing advancements, TDU for integrating Ayurveda with modern biology, and BHU for a Tata fellowship in food science. It highlights the company's 'For Better Living' purpose, innovation, agility, and sustainability as a key strategic pillar, emphasizing sustainable sourcing, better nutrition, responsible consumption, efficient resource management, and proactive adaptation to industry trends and regulations to create lasting stakeholder value and reduce environmental impact.

structure.title: OUR ESG PARADIGM

It emphasizes the Tata Group's Code of Conduct as a guiding framework for ethical practices, and robust stakeholder engagement to identify material ESG priorities, develop strategy, mitigate risks, and unlock sustainable growth opportunities.

structure.title: ESG Strategy Pillars and Governance Framework
structure.summary: This page outlines the company's ESG strategy, 'For Better Living,' built on four pillars: Better Planet (environmental stewardship), Better Nutrition (diverse nutritious options), Better Communities (strengthening stakeholders), and Better Sourcing (ethical, sustainable practices). It details KPIs aligned with global standards, a robust ESG governance structure ensuring accountability and transparency, and the mission to embed the strategy across the organization and value chain to strengthen the brand, expand market reach, and drive product innovation. The page also includes report sections like Delivering on Strategy, Financial Statements, Corporate Portrait, Business Momentum, Sustainability, Sustaining Value, and Statutory Reports.

structure.title: PERFORMANCE HIGHLIGHTS
structure.summary: The text highlights FY'25 performance with 29% of product launches health-focused and a new 'For Better' Nutrition Policy. It states the vision to improve access to healthy, natural, safe food. Targets include reaching 250 million Indian households by 2030 and 100% sustainable products by volume by 2040, with sustainability defined. It notes growing consumer demand for wellness products, the company's stringent quality norms, diverse tasty products meeting health and convenience needs, and pursuit of organic and inorganic growth to expand the portfolio and enhance public health impact.

structure.title: ENSURING ACCESS TO BETTER NUTRITION
structure.summary: The 'For Better Nutrition' pillar focuses on affordable, nutrient-enriched products, consumer insights, transparency, quality standards, and sustainable product stewardship. The FY 2023-24 policy, grounded in nutrition science and government recommendations, sets guidelines for ingredients, nutrients, and claims based on five principles: improving nutrition scores, aligning with public health recommendations, strengthening micronutrient profiles, using diverse ingredients for cleaner labels, and addressing hydration. Products are categorized into Superior Experiences (25-30%), Nutritionally Enhanced (8-10%), and Sustenance (60-65%). An Advisory Committee governs policy application and communications. Key areas include developing affordable products, digital consumer education, collaborating with nutritionists, and strategic partnerships. TCP participates in multi-stakeholder initiatives like FICCI to promote nutrition standards and data-driven policies. Recent acquisitions of Capital Foods and Organic India boosted the portfolio. The guiding principle ensures continuous nutrition enhancement and adapts to consumer needs for a healthier, sustainable India.

structure.title: ENRICHING THE NUTRIENT PROFILE
structure.summary: TCP emphasizes transparency with clear nutritional information exceeding regulations and aligns product development with FSSAI's Eat Right initiative for safe, healthy, sustainable food. It implements 'For Better' Food Ingredient guidelines evaluating ingredients like PHVO, refined sugars/flours, whole grains, legumes, millets, nuts, prebiotics, probiotics, herbs, botanicals, and additives, and 'For Better' Nutrient guardrails optimizing trans-fats, saturated fats, sodium, sugar, total fat, energy, protein, fiber, and micronutrients. Using WHO guidelines, FSSAI/ICMR daily values, product positioning, and portion sizes, category-level guardrails were set, benchmarked to industry standards, creating portfolio-wide thresholds for nutrients of concern. Internal and FSSAI claims criteria are defined, the portfolio is mapped, and reformulation progress is monitored, reinforcing commitment to healthier products.

structure.title: For Better' FY 2024-25 Nutrient Guardrails
structure.summary: This text outlines Tata Consumer Products' strategy for delivering better nutrition, including corporate portrait and business momentum. It details FY 2024-25 nutrient guardrails for nutrients of concern (trans fat, added sugars, total fat, sodium, SAFA) and positive nutrients (fiber, protein) with thresholds, plus fortification with micronutrients, botanicals, and pre/probiotics, and claims criteria. It discusses addressing nutritional gaps by enriching everyday essentials, integrating positive nutrition (whole grains, millets, pulses, etc.), and notes that about 1/5 of products are rich in protein and 15-18% in fiber, citing new products. It covers tailored regional enrichment, transparent labeling with FSSAI/RDI alignment, back-of-pack nutritional information, front-of-pack highlights, and meeting national and international safety and nutrition benchmarks.

structure.title: MAKING NUTRITION MORE AFFORDABLE
structure.summary: The text covers two main areas: affordable nutrition and consumer responsibility. It details efforts to make nutritious products affordable across socio-economic groups, including fortified tea with Vitamin C, zinc- and iodine-fortified salt, and double-fortified salt with iron and iodine to combat anaemia, while maintaining competitive prices. It also highlights consumer responsibility through transparent labeling—back-of-pack ingredient lists, Guideline Daily Amounts (GDAs), Reference Intake (RI) information, front-of-pack highlights of benefits like high fiber/protein, and 'For Better Claims Guidelines' covering sensory, ingredient, nutrient, and processing claims—to empower informed dietary choices without compromising taste.

It details R&D efforts with 54 professionals and four centers (Bengaluru, Mumbai, Barabanki, Sri City) focusing on health and nutrition innovation. Five health focus areas are identified: gut health, blood sugar management, protein delivery, sugar reduction, and iron supplementation. Strict guidelines for Nutritionally Enhanced products exclude artificial additives and refined ingredients, promoting whole grains and botanicals. Claims follow FSSAI guidelines. The text highlights double-fortified salt (iodine and iron) to combat malnutrition, and sugar/salt reduction initiatives, including a 30% and 20% added sugar reduction in RTD variants and ~2900 tons of sugar reduced since the policy's inception.

Specific examples include Tata Sampann Unpolished Dal for nutrition and Organic India products highlighting herbal benefits. structure.title: Better Sourcing: Sustainability, Stakeholders, and Targets

structure.title: VALUE CHAIN MANAGEMENT

structure.title: 1. Economic Review
structure.summary: The text provides an economic review covering global and Indian contexts. Globally, it discusses 2024's moderate 3.3% growth amid geopolitical tensions and high interest rates, with steady FMCG demand. The 2025 outlook forecasts slower 2.8% growth due to tariffs, recovering to 3% in 2026, with emerging markets as key drivers. It highlights opportunities from easing inflation, digital adoption, and supply chain resilience, while acknowledging risks. For India, it notes 6.5% GDP growth in FY25 driven by consumption and reforms, with a positive FMCG outlook for 2025 focusing on rural markets, premiumization, e-commerce, and sustainability. The company expresses confidence in leveraging these trends for growth through digital transformation and innovation.

structure.title: 2. Strategic Priorities
structure.summary: This section outlines Tata Consumer Products' strategic priorities: overall strategy focusing on core business strengthening, growth acceleration, sustainability, digital innovation, synergies, and future-ready organization; opportunities and strengths including market leadership in tea and salt, distribution, premiumization, global presence, and portfolio optimization; external threats and mitigation strategies covering market risks, raw material supply, competition, and regulatory compliance; growth drivers across India, International, and Non-Branded segments with details on product categories, distribution, digital initiatives, and acquisitions; the road ahead emphasizing sustainable profitable growth, brand investments, distribution expansion, premiumization, innovation, and cost savings; and sustainability strategy 'For Better Living' with four pillars, FY26 commitments, recognitions, sourcing, community, and planet initiatives.

nodes.title: 2.1 Overall Strategy
nodes.summary: The text outlines Tata Consumer Products' strategic priorities, covering overall strategy, brand portfolio, global presence, and market leadership in tea and salt. It details financial growth, distribution expansion, legal simplification, acquisitions, and new channel pilots. Operational enhancements include sales infrastructure, digital tools like MAVIC and ARS, and innovation with 41 new products. Sustainability achievements and Starbucks expansion are noted. The board refreshed strategic priorities to strengthen core business, accelerate growth, embed sustainability, drive digital and innovation, unlock synergies, and create a future-ready organization, with emphasis on execution excellence and new opportunities.

nodes.title: 2.2 Opportunities and Strengths
nodes.summary: The text outlines the company's leading market positions in Tea and Salt, with goals for growth through distribution, innovation, premiumization, and cost optimization. Strengths in distribution, operations, and customer engagement provide a platform for new ventures like Packaged Food, RTD beverages, cereals, snacks, and supplements, along with entry into Food Services and Pharmacy. It highlights global presence with Tetley and Eight O'Clock, premium brands like Teapigs and Good Earth, and strategies to safeguard black tea while expanding non-black tea and food portfolios internationally. The company leverages consumer trends toward wellness, sustainability, and premiumization, and pursues portfolio optimization, restructuring post-demerger with Tata Coffee, and supply chain efficiency recognized by ISCM, with plant accolades for energy efficiency, safety, and sustainability.

nodes.title: 2.3 External Threats and Mitigation Strategies
nodes.summary: The text discusses external threats and mitigation strategies, covering market risks and rural consumption trends, an omnichannel strategy for urban and rural markets, a diverse product portfolio with quality enhancements in tea and salt and growth businesses targeting premium segments, raw material supply risks from agricultural commodity price fluctuations due to global trends, geopolitical events, speculative trading, government policies, and supply chain issues, mitigated by a geographically diverse manufacturing footprint, broad vendor base, and systems like Infiniti and Arkieva for procurement monitoring, competition from regional and local players addressed through agility, quality, consumer centricity, and innovation, regulatory compliance via food safety measures, rigorous testing, careful ingredient use, substantiated claims, and adherence to evolving regulations on product, packaging, communication, and sustainability, and overall strategic imperatives to navigate challenges, mitigate risks, and capture opportunities.

nodes.title: 2.4 Growth Drivers
nodes.summary: The text covers growth drivers across India, International, and Non-Branded segments. In India, overall business growth is detailed with expansion to 275+ million households, 10x portfolio growth in 5 years, 41 new launches, distribution expansion, digital initiatives like ARS, and integration of Organic India and Capital Foods. Beverages section includes Tea (20% market share, innovation, premiumization, health portfolio), Coffee (Tata Coffee Grand crossing Rs. 100 Cr, RTD focus), and RTD (Tata Copper+, Himalayan, innovations, distribution). Foods covers Tata Salt leadership, value-added salts, Tata Sampann double-digit growth, and Capital Foods addition. Tata Starbucks added 58 stores. International covers UK, US, Canada, South Africa, Bangladesh, and Capital Foods launch. Non-Branded covers solubles restructuring and plantations.

nodes.title: 2.5 Road Ahead
nodes.summary:
2.5 Road Ahead
Tata Consumer Products will persist in driving sustainable and profitable growth by focusing on expanding its core markets in India and internationally, while also rapidly scaling new growth businesses. This effort will be supported by increased brand investments and enhanced distribution networks. Premiumization and innovation will be crucial in fueling this growth. Additionally, the Company will maintain a clear focus on executing cost-saving initiatives, including unlocking synergies through legal and organizational restructuring, to support the business.

nodes.title: 2.6 Sustainability
nodes.summary: Tata Consumer Products outlines its sustainability strategy 'For Better Living' based on four pillars: better sourcing, planet, communities, and nutrition. FY26 commitments include Scope 1 and 2 neutrality, 35% renewable energy, zero waste to landfill, and 70% recyclable packaging (already 72%). Recognitions include S&P Global Sustainability Yearbook 2025, Business World's Most Sustainable Consumer Goods Company, improved ESG risk rating, MSCI A rating, and CDP B ratings. Sourcing initiatives feature Rainforest Alliance and trustea certifications, C.A.F.E. Practices, Ethical Tea Partnership, and the Mthunzi initiative. Community efforts target 1.75 million beneficiaries by 2026 (1.51 million reached), affordable healthcare, and Project Jalodari. Planet initiatives include GHG reduction, renewable energy, TCFD and TNFD assessments, and circularity via compliance, smart packaging, and peer interaction, including a reuse strategy for Tata Salt bags.

structure.title: 3. Industry and Business Overview
structure.summary: The section provides an industry and business overview of Tata Consumer Products, covering India's packaged foods and beverages industry, including resilience amid inflation, growth drivers, and segment details like tea, coffee, RTD beverages, salt, pantry platform, mini-meals, Desi Chinese, and health supplements. It details business performance with net revenue growth, market share, innovations, and distribution expansion. The international business section discusses tea and coffee performance in the UK, US, and Canada, non-branded business growth driven by plantations and solubles, and Tata Starbucks expansion. The non-branded business grew 21%, and Tata Starbucks expanded to 479 stores with a target of 1,000 stores by FY28.

nodes.title: a) Industry overview and Outlook

nodes.title: b) Business Performance
nodes.summary: The text covers business performance across multiple categories: Tea grew 3% in net revenue with premium brands driving volume, expanded direct reach to 2.0 million outlets, and launched new products and campaigns like Jaago Re and Tata Tea Premium Care. Coffee grew 33%, with Tata Coffee crossing Rs. 100 Crores. Ready-to-Drink Beverages revenue grew 2% despite weather challenges, with Tata Copper Plus up 18% and Himalayan up 10%, premiumization via Tetley Kombucha and cold coffee. Salt maintained leadership with 37.2% market share, grew 4% in volume and 8% in value, and innovations like Sendha+ relaunch. Pantry Platform (Tata Sampann) grew 29%, with dry fruits and cold press oils crossing turnover milestones. Mini-meals (Tata Soulfull) grew 32%, launching Rusk and Masala Muesli. Desi Chinese (Capital Foods) grew 23% like-to-like, with innovations and campaigns. Health Supplements (Organic India) integration completed, showing growth in e-commerce and categories. The road ahead focuses on distribution-led growth, innovation, and cost savings.

structure.summary: The text outlines the Company's risk management framework. The ERM team collaborates with business functions to identify emerging risks and develop mitigation strategies. nodes.title: (c) Biological Assets
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting for biological assets and intangible assets. Biological assets are classified as bearer or consumable; tea bushes and shade trees are bearer assets, further split into mature and immature, carried at historical cost less depreciation and impairment, with capitalization of new plantations and depreciation over 50 years, and tea harvested measured at fair value less costs to sell with changes in profit or loss. nodes.title: (ii) Brands and Trademarks
nodes.summary: The text outlines accounting policies for brands/trademarks: initial measurement at fair value for separately acquired assets; subsequent carrying at cost less amortisation and impairment; recognition in business combinations outside goodwill if separable or from legal rights and reliably measurable. Useful lives are assessed as finite or indefinite, with finite lives amortised straight-line over 10-15 years. Impairment reviews occur for both finite and indefinite lives when indicators exist, and indefinite-life assets are tested periodically individually or as part of a cash-generating unit, not amortised, with annual reassessment of indefinite status and prospective change to finite if unsupportable.

nodes.title: (iii) Customer relationships
nodes.summary: The text outlines accounting policies for customer relationships and distribution networks acquired in business combinations, including fair value recognition, finite useful lives, and straight-line amortization over 8-20 and 8-10 years respectively. It covers patent/knowhow amortization over 10 years, and computer software capitalization criteria and amortization over 3-8 years for development costs and acquired licenses. Research and development policy distinguishes expensed research from capitalized development meeting specific criteria, with amortization over expected benefits and annual impairment testing during development. Impairment of tangible and intangible assets is discussed, including annual testing for indefinite-life assets. Finally, criteria for classifying non-current assets held for sale and disposal groups are mentioned.

nodes.title: Intangible Assets Accounting Policies and Impairment Review
key_items: Impairment of tangible and intangible assets
nodes.summary: The page outlines accounting policies for intangible assets: customer intangibles amortized over 8-20 years; distribution networks over 8-10 years; product development costs over 10 years; and computer software costs capitalized only if feasibility criteria are met, amortized over 3-8 years, with acquired licenses treated similarly. Research costs are expensed, while development costs are capitalized if criteria are met, amortized over expected benefit period, and tested annually for impairment during development. Tangible and intangible assets are reviewed for impairment when indicators exist, with impairment losses recognized for excess of carrying amount over recoverable amount, assets grouped into cash-generating units, prior impairments reviewed for reversal, and indefinite-lived or not-ready-to-use intangibles tested annually for impairment.

nodes.title: Assets held for sale and disposal groups
nodes.summary: The text covers non-current assets held for sale and disposal groups, including criteria for separate presentation in the balance sheet (commitment to sell, immediate availability, active sale plan, expected completion within 12 months), measurement at lower of carrying amount and fair value less cost to sell, and cessation of depreciation/amortization. It then introduces financial instruments, defining them and detailing financial assets: initial recognition at fair value (plus transaction costs unless at fair value through profit or loss), trade receivables at transaction price. It specifies investments in subsidiaries, associates, and joint ventures at cost less impairment, with impairment write-downs and disposal gains/losses in profit or loss. Subsequent measurement of debt instruments is classified into amortised cost (using effective interest rate method, with impairment losses in profit or loss) and fair value through other comprehensive income (FVTOCI, with fair value movements in OCI, interest income using EIR, impairment in profit or loss, and reclassification of cumulative gain/loss on derecognition).

nodes.title: Standalone Financial Statements Notes: Financial Instruments and Investments
key_items: Investments in Subsidiaries, Associates and Joint Venture:
nodes.summary: The page covers accounting policies for held-for-sale assets, financial instruments, and investments. It details held-for-sale criteria, measurement at lower of carrying amount and fair value less costs to sell, and cessation of depreciation. For financial instruments, it defines them and outlines initial recognition and measurement of financial assets at fair value plus transaction costs (except for fair value through profit or loss, where costs are expensed, and trade receivables without significant financing component measured at transaction price). It also covers investments in subsidiaries, associates, and joint ventures at cost less impairment, with impairment assessment and recognition of disposal differences in profit or loss.

nodes.title: Subsequent measurement Debt Instruments:
nodes.summary: The text details the subsequent measurement of debt instruments based on the business model, categorizing financial assets into amortised cost, FVTOCI, and FVTPL, with explanations of measurement, income recognition, and impairment. It covers equity instruments measured at fair value with election for FVTOCI or FVTPL, derecognition principles for financial assets and liabilities, impairment of financial assets using expected credit losses, initial and subsequent measurement of financial liabilities, and derivative financial instruments and hedging activities including fair value and cash flow hedges, documentation, and accounting treatment.

nodes.title: Financial Instruments Accounting Policies: Assets, Liabilities, Recognition, Measurement, Impairment, Derecognition
nodes.summary: The page presents accounting policies for financial instruments under Ind AS 109. It covers equity instruments measured at fair value with irrevocable FVTOCI or FVTPL election, and dividend recognition. Derecognition of financial assets occurs when contractual rights expire or are transferred. Impairment of financial assets uses expected credit losses based on past recovery, counterparty creditworthiness, and market conditions, with a simplified approach for trade receivables. Financial liabilities are initially recognized at fair value net of directly attributable costs, subsequently measured at amortized cost using the effective interest method, or at FVTPL with changes in profit or loss; short-term payables approximate fair value. Financial liabilities are derecognized when obligations are discharged, cancelled, or expired.

nodes.title: Derivative financial instruments and hedging activities
nodes.summary: The text covers derivative financial instruments and hedging activities, including initial recognition at fair value, subsequent remeasurement, and designation as fair value or cash flow hedges. It details documentation of hedging relationships, effectiveness assessment, and accounting for hedging reserve movements in other comprehensive income. It explains fair value hedge accounting for foreign exchange risk and cash flow hedge treatment of effective and ineffective portions, including reclassification upon hedge expiry or forecasted transaction changes. It outlines fair value measurement hierarchy (Levels 1, 2, 3) and offsetting criteria for financial assets and liabilities. Finally, it addresses interest income recognition using the effective interest method, impairment treatment, and dividend income recognition on an accrual basis.

nodes.title: Derivative Hedging, Fair Value Measurement, and Offsetting
nodes.summary: This page covers derivative accounting and financial instrument measurement: fair value hedges (changes in derivatives and hedged items recognized in profit or loss, applied only to foreign exchange risk on recognized assets/liabilities); cash flow hedges (effective portion in OCI, ineffective portion in profit or loss, with gains/losses reclassified when hedged items affect profit or loss, and rules for expiry, discontinuation, and forecasted transactions no longer expected); fair value hierarchy (Level 1 quoted prices, Level 2 observable inputs via valuation techniques, Level 3 unobservable entity-specific inputs); and offsetting of financial assets and liabilities (net reporting when legally enforceable right and intention to settle net or simultaneously exist, with right not contingent on future events and enforceable in normal business and default/insolvency/bankruptcy).

nodes.title: Interest and dividend income
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies for interest and dividend income, inventories, and employee benefits. Interest income is recognized using the effective interest method, including impaired loans. Dividend income is recognized when the right to receive payment is established, with investments on an accrual basis. Inventories are valued at lower of cost and net realizable value, with cost determined by weighted average or actual cost for teas, and agricultural produce measured at fair value less costs to sell. Employee benefits include post-employment schemes (defined benefit and contribution plans, medical plans), short-term and long-term benefits, other employee benefits like compensated absences, and termination benefits, with recognition and measurement bases specified.

nodes.title: Inventory Valuation and Employee Benefit Accounting Policies
nodes.summary: The page outlines accounting policies for inventories and employee benefits. Inventories of raw materials, traded and finished goods are valued at lower of cost or net realizable value, with stores and spares at cost and provisions for obsolete stock. Cost is weighted average except for teas at actual cost, including overheads, and agricultural produce is measured at fair value less costs to sell per Ind AS 41. Employee benefits cover defined benefit and contribution plans; short-term benefits are undiscounted, long-term discounted. Post-retirement benefits include PF, superannuation, gratuity, pension, and medical benefits, accounted on accrual or actuarial valuation, with remeasurements in OCI and interest in finance cost. Other benefits like compensated absences are accrued based on actuarial valuation.

nodes.title: Employee termination benefits:
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies for employee termination benefits, including recognition and measurement, and share-based payments under Ind AS 102. It details provisions, contingent liabilities, and contingent assets recognition and disclosure. It also covers income tax, distinguishing current tax measured under the Income Tax Act, 1961, and deferred tax using the balance sheet approach, including recognition of deferred tax assets and applicable tax rates.

nodes.title: Notes on Share-Based Payments, Provisions, Contingent Items, and Income Tax
key_items: Provisions, Contingent Liabilities and Contingent Assets
nodes.summary: This page from the Notes to Standalone Financial Statements covers accounting policies for termination benefits under AS 37, share-based payments under Ind AS 102 (recognizing compensation expense based on grant-date fair value over vesting period), provisions (recognized for present obligations with probable outflow and reliable estimate, measured at best estimate, reviewed and discounted if material), contingent liabilities (disclosed unless remote), contingent assets (not recognized until virtually certain but disclosed if inflow possible), and current income tax (measured per Income Tax Act, 1961).

nodes.title: ii) Deferred Tax:
nodes.summary: The text covers deferred tax recognition using the balance sheet approach, including temporary differences, tax rates, and offsetting rules. It details foreign currency translation, distinguishing functional and presentation currency, and accounting for foreign currency transactions and balances. Revenue from contracts with customers is explained, covering performance obligations, transaction price measurement, variable consideration, refund liabilities, and incremental costs. Government grants are addressed, including recognition, presentation, and deferred income for asset-related grants. Finally, lease assessment as a lessee is introduced, focusing on whether a contract conveys the right to control an identified asset.

nodes.title: Standalone Financial Statement Notes: Taxes, Foreign Currency, Revenue, Grants

It also includes report branding such as 'Delivering on Strategy', 'Corporate Portrait', and 'Business Momentum'.

nodes.title: Leases As a lessee
nodes.summary: The text covers lease accounting as a lessee and lessor, including lease identification criteria, recognition of right-of-use assets and lease liabilities, exemptions for short-term and low-value leases, treatment of extension/termination options, measurement and depreciation of ROU assets, impairment, and operating lease income recognition. It also addresses borrowing costs, including capitalization criteria, exceptional items disclosure, and basic and diluted earnings per share calculation.

nodes.title: Leases, Borrowing Costs, Exceptional Items, and Earnings Per Share Accounting Policies
nodes.summary: This page presents accounting policies: lessee recognition of right-of-use assets and lease liabilities, including short-term and low-value lease exemptions, extension/termination options, discounting, remeasurement, finance cost allocation, depreciation, and impairment; lessor recognition of operating lease income; borrowing costs definition and capitalization criteria; exceptional items disclosure; and basic and diluted earnings per share calculation methodologies.

nodes.title: Accounting Policies: Segment Reporting, Events, Goodwill, Depreciation

nodes.title: Employee Benefits

nodes.title: (d) Fair value of derivatives and other financial instruments
nodes.summary: The text covers fair value determination for derivatives and financial instruments under Ind AS 109 and 113, including valuation methods for unlisted instruments; recent accounting pronouncements noting no new standards notified by MCA for the year ended March 31, 2025; and detailed property, plant and equipment schedules showing cost, accumulated depreciation, impairment, disposals, and net carrying value for land, buildings, plant and equipment, furniture, motor vehicles, and office equipment, along with footnotes on leased plantation land, building costs represented by shares, and leasehold land.

nodes.title: Financial Risk Disclosures: Interest Rate and Price Risk
nodes.summary: The page presents notes to standalone financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2025, focusing on two financial risk types. Interest rate risk is defined as the risk that fair value or future cash flows of a financial instrument will fluctuate due to changes in market interest rates, and it can also impact retiral benefit provisions. The Company primarily uses fixed-rate borrowings, so it is not subject to interest rate risk because neither carrying amounts nor future cash flows fluctuate with market rates, and it is not significantly exposed at reporting dates. Price risk arises from investments classified as fair value through other comprehensive income or profit or loss. Equity investments are mainly strategic and long-term, while current investments are in liquid mutual fund units, both not exposed to significant price risk.
