It then describes the equity method for accounting investments in associates and joint ventures, including initial cost recognition, adjustments for post-acquisition profits, other comprehensive income, dividends, and elimination of unrealized gains and losses. It also covers impairment assessment at each reporting date, comparing recoverable amount to carrying amount and recognizing impairment in profit or loss, along with a reference to material accounting policies applied consistently.

nodes.title: (a) Business Combinations
nodes.summary: The text details the Group's accounting for business combinations using the acquisition method, covering consideration components (fair values of assets transferred, liabilities incurred, equity interests issued, contingent consideration), initial measurement of identifiable assets/liabilities at fair value, goodwill recognition (or gain to equity/capital reserve for bargain purchases), non-controlling interest at fair value, equity transactions for ownership changes without control loss, put/call options for non-controlling interests (liability at present value with equity charge), common control combinations using pooling of interest (carrying amounts with policy harmonization), expensing acquisition-related costs, step acquisitions with remeasurement of previously held interests, provisional accounting with measurement period up to one year, and contingent consideration recognition at fair value with subsequent changes in profit or loss (unless equity-classified).

nodes.title: (b) Property, Plant and Equipment
nodes.summary: This text covers accounting policies for property, plant, and equipment (PPE) including bearer assets. It details recognition and measurement at historical cost less depreciation and impairment, including treatment of subsequent expenditure, replacements, repairs, maintenance, and assets under development. Depreciation policies are outlined: amortization over useful lives per Schedule II of the Companies Act, 2013 or technical evaluation, straight-line basis, land not depreciated, periodic review of residual values and useful lives, impairment writedowns to recoverable amount, and recognition of disposal gains/losses. A table provides estimated useful lives for leasehold improvements, buildings, plant and machinery, furniture/fixtures/office equipment, and motor vehicles.

nodes.title: (c) Biological Assets
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies for biological assets, investment property, and intangible assets. Biological assets are split into bearer and consumable, with bearer plants (tea, coffee, pepper, shade trees) classified as mature or immature, carried at historical cost less depreciation and impairment, with new plantation costs capitalized and immature areas transferred to mature plantations and depreciated over 30–58 years. Agricultural produce (tea, coffee, pepper, minor crops) is measured at fair value less cost to sell at harvest, with changes in profit or loss. Investment property, held for rental or capital appreciation, is initially at cost, subsequently at cost less depreciation and impairment, depreciated straight-line over 60 years, with assets under development not depreciated. Intangible assets include goodwill arising from business combinations, allocated to CGUs for annual impairment testing, not amortized, with impairment recognized and not reversed unless held for sale; and brands/trademarks measured initially at fair value, carried at cost less amortization and impairment.

nodes.title: Accounting Policies for Investment Property and Goodwill
nodes.summary: The page outlines accounting policies for bearer assets, investment property, and goodwill. Expenditure on bearer assets is capitalized when future benefits are probable and measurable; immature plantations are capitalized and transferred to mature plantations depreciated over 30-58 years. Agricultural produce (tea, coffee, pepper, minor crops) is measured at fair value less costs to sell, with changes recognized in profit or loss. Investment property, held for rental or capital appreciation, is initially at cost, subsequently at cost less depreciation and impairment, with subsequent expenditure capitalized when probable and measurable, depreciated straight-line over 60 years, and assets under development not depreciated until ready. Goodwill from business combinations is the excess of fair value of consideration over identifiable net assets, allocated to cash-generating units for impairment testing, not amortized but tested annually, with impairment recognized immediately and not reversed unless specific conditions apply.

nodes.title: (ii) Brands and Trademarks
nodes.summary: The text outlines accounting policies for intangible assets: brands/trademarks (initial measurement, finite/indefinite useful lives, amortization, impairment testing), customer relationships (fair value at acquisition, finite lives of 8-20 years), distribution networks (fair value, finite lives of 8-10 years), patent/knowhow (product development costs amortized over 10 years), computer software (capitalization criteria, amortization over 3-8 years, website costs), and research and development (research expensed, development expenditure discussed).

nodes.title: Intangible Assets Accounting Policies and Useful Lives
nodes.summary: The page outlines accounting policies for intangible assets: brands/trademarks with finite or indefinite lives, including impairment testing and amortization over 10–25 years; customer relationships recognized at fair value with 8–20 year lives; distribution networks with 8–10 year lives; product development costs (patents/knowhow) amortized over 10 years; and computer software, covering capitalization criteria for development costs and websites, and amortization over 3–8 years for software and licenses. All finite-lived intangibles are amortized on a straight-line basis and reviewed for impairment.

nodes.title: (vii) Research and Development
nodes.summary: The text outlines accounting policies for research and development, impairment of tangible and intangible assets, and financial instruments. Research costs are expensed as incurred, while development costs are capitalized only if specific criteria are met, then amortized and tested for impairment annually. Impairment of depreciable/amortizable assets is reviewed when indicators exist, with losses measured as the excess of carrying amount over recoverable amount; non-financial asset impairments may be reversed, while indefinite-life or not-ready-to-use intangibles are tested annually. Financial instruments are defined, and financial assets are initially measured at fair value (plus transaction costs unless at fair value through profit or loss, with trade receivables at transaction price). Debt instruments are subsequently classified as amortized cost (using effective interest method) or fair value through other comprehensive income, with corresponding treatment of interest income and impairment losses.

nodes.title: Accounting Policies for Assets and Financial Instruments
key_items: Impairment of tangible and intangible assets
nodes.summary: The page covers development expenditure capitalization and amortization, impairment of tangible and intangible assets, definition of financial instruments, and initial recognition and measurement of financial assets. It details criteria for capitalizing development costs, impairment review triggers and measurement, reversal of impairments, and annual testing for indefinite-life intangibles. It defines financial instruments and explains initial measurement at fair value plus transaction costs, with exceptions for fair value through profit or loss and trade receivables without significant financing component.

nodes.title: Subsequent measurement Debt Instruments:
nodes.summary: This text covers the Group's accounting policies for financial instruments. It details subsequent measurement of debt instruments, classifying them into amortised cost, FVTOCI, and FVTPL, with respective measurement methods, income recognition, and impairment treatment. Equity instruments are measured at fair value with an irrevocable election for FVTOCI or FVTPL, including dividend and gain/loss recognition. It also addresses derecognition criteria for financial assets, impairment methodology using expected credit losses, financial liabilities' initial and subsequent measurement (amortised cost or FVTPL) and derecognition, and derivative financial instruments and hedging activities, including hedge types and documentation requirements.

nodes.title: Financial Instruments Accounting Policies and Measurements
nodes.summary: The page covers accounting policies for financial instruments: equity instruments measured at fair value with elections for FVTOCI or FVTPL, including OCI treatment and dividend recognition; derecognition of financial assets when rights expire or are transferred; impairment of financial assets using expected credit losses based on recovery history, credit-worthiness, and market conditions, with simplified approach for trade receivables; financial liabilities initially recognized at fair value net of costs, subsequently at amortized cost or FVTPL, with derecognition upon discharge, cancellation, or expiry.

nodes.title: Derivative financial instruments and hedging activities
nodes.summary: The text covers derivative financial instruments and hedging activities, including initial recognition at fair value and subsequent re-measurement, designation as fair value or cash flow hedges, documentation of hedging relationships and effectiveness assessments. It details accounting for movements in hedging reserves, classification of hedging derivatives as current or non-current based on maturity, and specific treatments for fair value hedges (gains/losses in profit or loss) and cash flow hedges (effective portion in other comprehensive income, ineffective in profit or loss, reclassification to profit or loss when hedged item affects profit or loss, and handling of expired or discontinued hedges). It also covers fair value measurement hierarchy (Levels 1, 2, 3), offsetting financial instruments conditions, and interest and dividend income recognition, including treatment for impaired loans.

nodes.title: Hedge Accounting, Fair Value Measurement, and Offsetting Financial Instruments
nodes.summary: This page covers hedge accounting policies including fair value hedges and cash flow hedges, detailing recognition, classification, and treatment of gains/losses. It also addresses fair value measurement hierarchy (Levels 1, 2, and 3) and offsetting financial instruments criteria.

nodes.title: Interest and dividend income
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies for interest and dividend income, inventories, and employee benefits. Interest income is recognized using the effective interest method, including for impaired loans. Dividend income is recognized when the right to receive payment is established. Inventories are valued at lower of cost or net realizable value, with cost determined by weighted average (except auction teas at actual cost). Agricultural produce is measured at fair value less costs to sell. Employee benefits include post-employment schemes (defined benefit and contribution plans) accounted on accrual basis with actuarial valuations, other employee benefits like compensated absences, and termination benefits recognized when incurred.

nodes.title: Accounting Policies for Inventories and Employee Benefits
nodes.summary: The page covers accounting policies for dividend income, inventories, and employee benefits. Inventories are valued at lower of cost or net realizable value, with cost determined by weighted average or actual cost for teas, and agricultural produce measured at fair value less costs to sell. Employee benefits include post-employment schemes (defined benefit and contribution plans, PF, superannuation, gratuity, pension, medical) accounted on accrual or actuarial valuation, with remeasurements in other comprehensive income. Other employee benefits like compensated absences are accrued based on actuarial valuation.

nodes.title: Employee termination benefits:
nodes.summary: The text covers employee termination benefits, including payment timing, recognition criteria, measurement for voluntary redundancy, and discounting; share-based payments under Ind AS 102, detailing fair value expense recognition; provisions, contingent liabilities, and contingent assets, with recognition, measurement, and disclosure principles; and income tax, distinguishing current tax measured per local laws and deferred tax using the balance sheet approach, including recognition of deferred tax assets and tax items in equity.

nodes.title: Notes on Share-Based Payments, Provisions, Contingent Items, and Income Tax
key_items: Provisions, Contingent Liabilities and Contingent Assets
nodes.summary: The page covers several notes to consolidated financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2025. It addresses termination benefits, including timing of recognition and measurement. Share-based payments are recognized per Ind AS 102, with fair value charged over vesting period. Provisions are recognized for present obligations, measured at best estimate, discounted if material, and reviewed at each reporting date. Contingent liabilities are possible obligations from past events, disclosed unless remote. Contingent assets are not recognized until virtually certain but disclosed if inflow is possible. Current income tax is measured at expected amount payable per local laws. The page also includes sections like Delivering on Strategy, Corporate Portrait, and Business Momentum, and is part of the Integrated Annual Report 2024-25.

nodes.title: ii) Deferred Tax:
nodes.summary: The text covers deferred tax accounting using the balance sheet approach for temporary differences between tax bases and carrying amounts. It details recognition of deferred tax assets based on probable taxable profit, use of enacted tax rates, recognition of current and deferred tax in equity for equity items, and special treatment for investments in subsidiaries and joint arrangements. It also explains offsetting of deferred tax assets and liabilities under legal and net settlement conditions. Finally, it introduces foreign currency translation, specifying functional currency measurement and presentation in Indian Rupees for the Parent Company.

nodes.title: ii) Group entities
nodes.summary:
ii) Group entities
The results and financial position of all the Group entities that have a functional currency different from the presentation currency of the Group are translated as follows:
- assets and liabilities for each balance sheet presented are translated at the closing rate at the date of that balance sheet;
- income and expenses for each statement of profit and loss are translated at monthly exchange rates, and
- all resulting exchange differences are recognised in other comprehensive income.
On disposal of a foreign operation, the associated exchange differences are reclassified to the statement of profit and loss, as part of the gain or loss on disposal.
Goodwill and fair value adjustments arising on the acquisition of a foreign entity are treated as assets and liabilities of the foreign entity and translated at the closing rate. Exchange differences arising are recognised in other comprehensive income.

nodes.title: (n) Revenue from contracts with customer
nodes.summary: The text covers revenue recognition from contracts with customers, including timing of satisfaction, measurement based on transaction price net of variable consideration, refund liabilities for returns, and capitalization of incremental contract costs. It also details government grant recognition, lease accounting for lessees (identifying leases, recognizing right-of-use assets and lease liabilities, short-term/low-value exemptions, remeasurement, depreciation, impairment) and lessors (operating lease income on straight-line basis), and borrowing costs (composition and capitalization for qualifying assets).

nodes.title: Accounting Policies: Government Grants and Leases
nodes.summary: The page outlines accounting policies for government grants and leases. Government grants, including non-monetary grants, are recognized when reasonable assurance exists that conditions will be met, and are systematically recognized in profit or loss over the periods when related costs are expensed. Grants related to property, plant, and equipment are presented at fair value and recognized as deferred income. For leases as a lessee, the Group assesses whether a contract contains a lease based on control of an identified asset. At commencement, right-of-use assets and lease liabilities are recognized for all leases except short-term (12 months or less) and low-value leases (under Rs 0.05 Crores), which are expensed on a straight-line basis. Lease liabilities are measured by discounting lease payments using the implicit interest rate or incremental borrowing rate, and remeasured for changes in extension or termination options. Right-of-use assets are initially at cost and subsequently depreciated on a straight-line basis over the shorter of useful life or lease term, with impairment assessed. As a lessor, operating lease income is recognized on a straight-line basis over the lease term.

nodes.title: (q) Borrowing Costs

Exceptional Items are separately disclosed when material and necessary for understanding financial performance. Earnings per share includes basic and diluted calculations, dividing profit or loss attributable to ordinary shareholders by weighted average shares, with diluted EPS adjusting for own shares and dilutive potential shares. Segment Reporting defines segments based on the CODM's resource allocation and performance review, includes segment results with directly attributable and reasonably allocable items, discloses unallocable items separately, and defines segment capital expenditure as total cost to acquire property, equipment, intangible assets, and goodwill.
